cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: One Thing Leads to Another
cards.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. This café chair wobbles. Let's take all the chairs apart and check their joints.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I tested them. It's only this chair, on this floorboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then we'll lift the floorboards. The chairs have exposed a flooring problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll close for renovations. Once the floor's up, we can move the counter and sort out the queue.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decides and A3 delays details, but A5 ordinary closure proposal does not distinctly continue approval over B practical concerns.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 isolated floorboard causes A3 floor removal; B4 opening deadline causes A5 closure and counter relocation, after unrelated restriction.

relationship.evidence: B2 has tested the chairs and B4 protects opening time, providing concrete attempts to limit unnecessary work.

heightening.evidence: B4 immediate operation concern becomes A5 a reason to close and undertake still broader changes.

specificity.evidence: A1 cafe chair, B2 floorboard and B4 twenty-minute opening establish the task and disruptive cost.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 queue redesign follows the opened floor opportunity, but the A3 stock authority phrase is clumsy.
